title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-scratchpad-18
content:
TL;DR: intermittent capacity thrash during dedicated GPU pool warmup. Scheduler rapidly spins up nodes then drains them because warmup probes time out / image pull delays + preemption on shared infra causing pool never to reach steady capacity; requests hit fallback which increases observed latency. Collected timeline + commands tried below.

Context:
- Dedicated pool: pool-ded-gpu-a, instance group size target 8 -> autoscale target increases to 24 during daily batch warmup window (03:00-04:00 UTC).
- Warmup job: warmup-daemonset v2.3 pulls model artifacts (~4.2GB) + runs kv-cache init; readiness probe waits for exit code 0 from /opt/warmup/finish.sh with 120s timeout.
- Symptoms: repeated spike in 'pending' requests, rapid node churn (~15-30m cycles), error snippets show "failed to allocate GPU context" and "OOM when allocating tensor" in some warmup pods.

Raw timeline (local notes):
- 2026-02-20 03:02 UTC: Autoscale triggered (scale-up to 24). Many new instances scheduled.
- 03:04 UTC: kubelet starts warmup pods, image pull backlog observed.
- 03:06 UTC: Several nodes fail healthcheck, GCE preempted some VMs (spot-like config).
- 03:09 UTC: IG manager marks nodes unhealthy -> removes then recreates -> churn.
- 03:15 UTC: A subset of warmup pods log "failed to allocate context: no devices available".
- 03:22 UTC: Autoscaler notices insufficient ready nodes and triggers another scale-up -> overshoot -> more churn.
- 03:45 UTC: Situation stabilizes after manual intervention (reduced autoscale aggressiveness, bumped readiness timeout to 300s).

Commands tried (snips):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=ded-gpu-a
  -> many nodes in NotReady/Unknown during window

- kubectl describe pod warmup-daemonset-xxxxx -n serving-runtime
  -> Events: Back-off pulling image; Readiness probe failed - timeout

- kubectl logs warmup-daemonset-xxxxx -n serving-runtime --previous
  -> "Model artifact download: 4.2GB start..."
  -> "[ERROR] failed to allocate context: cudaSetDevice failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY"

- gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'ded-gpu'" --zones=us-west1-*
  -> Several VMs preempted (status: TERMINATED) around 03:06

- gcloud compute instance-groups managed describe ig-ded-gpu-a --zone us-west1-a
  -> autohealing triggered due to failed health-checks (kubelet not ready)

- curl -sS http://prometheus.internal:9090/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[10m])
  -> spike correlated with autoscale events

- redis-cli LLEN warmup:queue (we use a small queue to coordinate preloads) -> values stayed small; suggests warmup isn't queued backlog problem

Hypotheses: (ordered by likelihood)
1) Image/artifact pull + model download time >> readiness probe timeout -> nodes marked unhealthy before warmup completes -> autoscaler sees low readiness and keeps adding nodes, creating feedback loop (thrash).
2) Preemptible/spot instance config causing GCE preemptions in window -> fractional nodes disappear mid-warmup increasing churn.
3) Warmup process OOMs when multiple warmup containers run concurrently on same GPU host (mis-specified resource limits or side processes leaking GPU memory).
4) Scheduler (cluster-autoscaler) and IG health-checks are tuned too tightly causing race between node.ready and instance health checks.

Mitigations tried (and results):
- Increased warmup readiness timeout from 120s -> 300s (PATCH applied): reduced churn in next window but not eliminated (still saw 2x fewer cycles).
- Set pre-pull images via daemonset init container (experimental): helped reduce image pull backlog by ~40% in synthetic test.
- Switched some node templates from preemptible -> on-demand for critical zone (manual): decreased preemption but cost spike.
- Added small sleep + GPU mem flush between warmup containers to avoid simultaneous full-memory allocations (local patch to warmup script): reduced OOM errors in test.
- Adjusted autoscaler scale-up limit: max surge -> +8 instead of +16. Result: fewer simultaneous new nodes; helped, but still slow steady state.

Open action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Run controlled experiment: repro at 03:00 window with on-demand instances only -> measure churn. (Evan to run)
- [ ] Add artifact checksum + resume download in warmup script to avoid full re-download on retry. (Maya)
- [ ] Improve readiness probe: move to a two-phase readiness (image+download -> containerReady; model init -> appReady) so IG health-checks don't mark node bad prematurely. (Alex)
- [ ] Add cluster-autoscaler annotation tuning to delay scale-down until X minutes after last scale-up (reduce oscillation). (SRE/infra)
- [ ] Create a canary pool with slower autoscale aggressiveness and test rollouts.

Notes/lessons:
- Warmup that assumes immediate GPU availability is brittle on cloud spot/preemptible mixes. We should make warmup resilient: resume downloads, avoid OOM by conservative allocation, and separate image pull from heavy GPU init.
- Autoscaler tuning matters: aggressive scale-up + tight health-checks -> feedback loop. We need guardrails (max surge, warm-up window, backoff) documented in runbook.

Quick runbook snippet (for on-call):
1) If pool thrashing observed during warmup window: temporarily reduce autoscale target to previous steady state (gcloud set-instance-group manager size X)
2) Increase warmup readiness timeout (kubectl patch ds warmup-daemonset -p '{"spec":{...}}')
3) Verify image pull backlog: kubectl get events --all-namespaces | grep "Back-off pulling image"
4) If preemptions seen: check billing/instance-template for preemptible flag; consider migrating critical zones to on-demand
5) Post-incident: open ENG ticket to add two-phase readiness + checkpointed downloads

Logs / useful snippets to attach to ticket: (copied to ENG-3421)
- pod logs: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY"
- instance-group events around 03:06 showing autohealing
- prometheus query snapshots for pod restart spikes

Notes for next run: instrument warmup-daemonset to emit metrics: download_progress_bytes, gpu_alloc_bytes, init_phase{stage}. Add annotation to pods to force node provisioning order (if possible).

End of scratchpad. Will convert to more formal incident summary if ENG-3421 reaches incident status.
